run.hint: This runs the original Python code in your browser. Nothing is sent to a server. The first start downloads the Python runtime (about 13 MB).

state.unsupported: Your browser blocks the feature this terminal needs. Try reloading the page or a current Chrome, Firefox or Safari.

how.inBrowser: The Python files are copied from my GitHub repo at a fixed commit and served by this site. When you press Run, your browser downloads Pyodide (CPython compiled to WebAssembly) and runs the program in a Web Worker, a separate thread, so the page stays responsive. The terminal is xterm.js. When the program calls input(), the worker sleeps on shared memory until you press Enter.
how.static: This project runs on its own, outside this site. The overview shows its README from GitHub.
how.runner: Runs go into a job queue in Postgres. A Python worker picks them up, runs them with a timeout and writes the result back; the page watches the job live.
how.bot: The bot runs on a small server and writes a heartbeat to the database after every check. This page only reads it.
how.simulator: The simulator is its own Python backend (FastAPI, Postgres, a worker) in a separate repo. It runs on a small server with no open ports. A run from this page goes into the site's job queue; the site's worker forwards it to the simulator over a private network and sends the result back. The dashboard reads a small snapshot that the simulator publishes once a day.

sim.sample: SAMPLE DATA · the simulator is still being built
sim.intro: Three model portfolios, picked by the simulator's rules and started with {amount} each on {start}. They are not changed by hand and are valued after every trading day, next to simply buying the S&P 500 ({benchmark}).
sim.performanceSummary: Line chart. The portfolio is now worth {value}, {change} since the start. {benchmark}: {benchmarkChange}.
sim.outlookSummary: Fan chart. After {years} years, 5 of 100 simulated paths end below {low}, the middle path ends at {mid}, and 5 of 100 end above {high}.
sim.outlookNote: Not a forecast. {paths} possible futures were built by reshuffling this portfolio's past daily returns. The bands show where most of them ended. This cannot show events that never happened in the data, and in a crash stocks tend to fall together more than their history suggests.
sim.disclaimer: This is a simulation for learning purposes. No real money is invested. Past performance says little about the future. Not financial advice.
sim.empty: The model portfolios have not started yet. The first numbers appear here once the simulator publishes its first daily snapshot.
